# 0044: A skill is invoked the way its user invokes it, in each harness's own syntax

Status: accepted, 2026-08-31. Refines
[0011](0011-inject-skill-through-each-cli-path.md) (the skill loads through each
CLI's own path) and
[0034](0034-a-harness-is-a-class-and-the-registry-is-the-only-dispatch.md) (a
harness is a class and the registry is the only dispatch). **Supersedes the
`prompt=` field of `@evalcase` established by
[0008](0008-evals-are-eval-prefixed-modules.md).** Breaking: `EvalCase.prompt`
becomes `EvalCase.task`, and `result.json`'s `case` record gains `task` beside
`prompt`.

## Context

0011 settled that a skill reaches the agent through each CLI's own loading path,
and the two adapters implemented it: Claude got `--add-dir <skill dir>`, Codex
got a copy into the private `CODEX_HOME/skills/`. Two different mechanisms, as
0011 intended.

But the *prompt* stayed one string, shared by every cell of the case, and it had
to paper over the difference the adapters had just introduced. Every case in
every consuming repository opened the same way:

> Use the mermaidjs-diagrams skill (its SKILL.md is in the extra allowed
> directory / your skills).

That sentence is the tell. "The extra allowed directory / your skills" is a
prompt written to survive two loading paths at once, and it names neither
mechanism correctly:

| What the prompt asked for | What actually happens |
| --- | --- |
| Claude: "its SKILL.md is in the extra allowed directory" | `--add-dir` grants *tool access* to a path. It does not register a skill. The agent has to be told a path, then read it as a file, then decide to follow it — three steps a real user never performs. |
| Codex: "/ your skills" | The skill *is* registered, and Codex's own instructions say the trigger is `$SkillName`. The prompt never used it, so the skill was reached by description-match at best. |

So the matrix's two arms were not running the same experiment. One arm graded a
skill loaded as a document; the other graded a skill loaded as a skill. Neither
arm graded what a user does, which is the only invocation whose failure anybody
would care about. A skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter is malformed — the single
most common way a skill breaks for its users — passed both arms, because being
told to read a file does not require the file to be registered.

Both CLIs have a documented, verified invocation, and they are not the same:

| Harness | Registration | Invocation a user types | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | `--plugin-dir <dir>`, where the dir carries `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `skills/<skill>/` | `/<skill> <task>` | claude 2.1.251, against `--setting-sources ""` |
| `codex` | a copy under the private `CODEX_HOME/skills/<skill>/` | `$<skill> <task>` | codex-cli 0.151.0, against `--ignore-user-config` |

Claude's `--add-dir` was never a registration; `--plugin-dir` is, and it is the
only one that keeps 0005's isolation intact — a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` would
take the credentials with it, and `--setting-sources user` needs them.

## Decision

**A case declares a task, not a prompt.** `@evalcase(task=...)` is the sentence a
user would type *after* naming the skill: "Apply the palette mandate to
ARCHITECTURE.md." It never names the skill, never names a loading path, and never
mentions a CLI.

**The harness renders the invocation.** `Harness.invoke(skill=, task=)` is a new
abstract member beside the four 0034 already requires, and it is the only place
either syntax is spelled: `claude` renders `/<skill> <task>`, `codex` renders
`$<skill> <task>`. Nothing outside `harness/` composes an invocation, so a third
CLI with a third syntax is still the one-file job 0034 promises. The one lookup
from underneath goes through `model/registry.py`, 0039's declared edge.

**Registration is the adapter's job, and it is real registration.** The Claude
adapter builds a wrapper plugin — `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` plus a copy of the
skill under `skills/` — beside the workspace, and passes `--plugin-dir`. A skill
whose frontmatter Claude rejects now fails the cell, which is the point.

**The rendered prompt is evidence.** `CaseRef` carries both: `task`, the case's
declaration, and `prompt`, the exact string that reached the CLI. A reader of one
`result.json` can see what was asked without holding the suite file, and two
cells of one case can be compared knowing precisely how their asks differed.

## Consequences

Every existing suite is a breaking change, and deliberately so: a `prompt=` that
still carries "use the X skill (its SKILL.md is in ...)" is exactly the text this
record exists to delete. `@evalcase` raises on `prompt=` with a message naming
`task=`, rather than accepting it as an alias — an alias would let the old
sentence survive the upgrade.

A cell can now fail for a reason it previously could not: the skill did not
resolve. That is a true negative. `/nosuchskill` comes back as "Unknown command"
with zero billed tokens, so the evidence gate of
[0045](0045-the-verifiers-ship-with-the-plugin.md) catches it before any grader
reads a workspace.

Captured runs from before this record carry `case.prompt` and no `case.task`; a
replay reads the task back as empty rather than re-deriving it, per
[0038](0038-a-tolerant-reader-still-honours-its-declaration.md).

Two things showed up only once the first live cell ran under a real invocation, and
both are consequences of registering the skill properly rather than describing it:

**The skill's own `evals/` tree was being handed to the agent under test.** Both
loading paths copy the skill directory, and since 0046 that directory contains the
goldens. The exclusion is now in the shared spawn contract (`harness/base.py`), not
in either adapter, so a third provider cannot reintroduce it.

**The dialects disagree about whether `SKILL.md` is ever *read*.** Same task, same
fixture: `claude` resolves `/<skill>` by injecting the file, so it never appears in
skill coverage, while `codex` is instructed to read it and so it does. An eval that
asserts `SKILL.md` was loaded therefore passes on one arm and fails on the other for
a reason that is not about the skill — which is precisely the failure this record
exists to end, reappearing one level down. `check_skill_was_loaded` has no default
and refuses an empty call; what a case names is the `resources/` and `scripts/`
material the entry point points at, which both dialects reach when they follow it.

## Lens

An eval that has to explain the harness to the agent is measuring the harness.
The prompt is not a place to reconcile two loading mechanisms — the reconciliation
belongs behind the interface that already exists to hold the difference, and what
the case declares is the part a user would actually say.
